By the greedy exchange argument, sorting both arrays produces an optimal one-to-one assignment in O(n log n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.
Sorting jobs and workers pairs larger workloads with larger capacities. Any crossed pairing a <= b with x <= y cannot beat (a, x) and (b, y) in completion time, proving sorted assignment optimality.

Sorting both arrays of length n takes O(n log n) time. Zipping and computing max duration takes O(n) time. Total time complexity is O(n log n) with O(n) space for sorting. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
